name: swarm
description: Fan a batch of independent, self-contained tasks out to nested agents running concurrently, each with its own context and a short iteration budget; returns once every member finishes. WHEN TO USE: several sub-problems that do not depend on each other's output and can run at once — checking a handful of unrelated files, drafting several independent patches, running the same check across several targets. WHEN NOT TO USE: a single task (use subagent instead), or tasks where a later one needs an earlier one's result (that is sequential, not parallel — do it yourself or chain subagent calls). Each task starts with an EMPTY transcript and cannot see the other members or your own transcript: write every task as a complete, standalone brief, the way you would for subagent. Members writing the same file race with no lock — give each task its own file, or say what not to touch. Input: {"tasks": ["...", "..."], "provider": "kimi-k3"}. Up to 8 tasks per call.
llm_description: Fan out up to 8 independent, self-contained tasks to nested agents running concurrently (each own context, short budget); returns when all finish. Use only for tasks with no interdependency (single task: use subagent; sequential/dependent: do it yourself or chain subagent calls). Each task needs an EMPTY-transcript-ready standalone brief; members writing the same file race with no lock. Input: {tasks: [...], provider?}.

tasks.description: Self-contained task briefs, one per nested agent, run concurrently. Up to 8.
